title: RBAC v2 + Audit Log Schema: SIEM Export and SOC2/ISO Control Mapping (auditor prep)
content:
Executive summary: This working doc outlines how RBAC v2 changes, the stabilized audit log schema, and our SIEM export format map to SOC 2 and ISO 27001 evidence. It contains a short control mapping, a prioritized gap analysis, SIEM query examples auditors commonly request, and a curated Q&A set to prep control owners for auditor interviews. Goal: produce a repeatable evidence packet (automated where possible) to shorten audit cycles and reduce ad-hoc evidence requests.

Scope: covers backend control-plane RBAC (role/permission model and admin change flows), API-level audit logs (authz/authn events, policy changes, policy evaluations), ingestion/export pipeline to our SIEM (JSON over S3 / Kafka -> SIEM), and the artifacts we use to demonstrate control operation during SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 assessments. Does NOT include endpoint telemetry (agent-level host logs) or third-party vendor controls (those are covered separately).

1) RBAC v2: notable design points relevant to auditors
- Role model: hierarchical roles + attribute-based grants; all grants are expressed as tuples (grantee, resource-pattern, action-set, grantor, timestamp, expiry).
- Admin approval: privilege-escalation requires two-step approval for prod-scoped roles (request -> approver 1 -> approver 2 / time-based auto-deny).
- Policy versioning: every policy change creates an immutable policy document with changelog id and author.
- Delegation & service roles: service-accounts (machine principals) are issued short-lived keys; policy binding recorded in audit log.

2) Audit log schema (standardized fields we now emit):
- event_ts (RFC3339 UTC)
- event_id (UUID v4)
- trace_id (for request correlation)
- request_id
- actor_id (user_id or service_id)
- actor_type (human | service | oauth-app)
- action (string: e.g., policy.create, role.assign, authz.check, token.issue)
- resource_type (e.g., project, model, route, key)
- resource_id (opaque id)
- policy_id (if applicable)
- before (short summary or checksum)
- after (short summary or checksum)
- outcome (allowed | denied | error)
- client_ip
- user_agent
- location (region tag)
- retention_tag (hot | cold | archived)
- raw_payload (full event body, base64 compressed)
- signed (boolean string)
Notes: we ship both compact JSON to SIEM and a gzipped archival payload to S3 for deep inspection. All admin actions include linked changelog ids.

3) SIEM export format and retention snapshot
- Export format: NDJSON (one JSON event per line) with schema above. We support two export sinks: (1) Real-time stream via Kafka -> SIEM (Elastic/QRadar) and (2) Batch export to S3 bucket for historic review.
- Enrichment applied prior to export: geolocation (from client_ip), principal_group (team, org), risk_score (simple heuristic for auth failures), and retention_policy label.
- Retention: hot (30d readily searchable), cold (365d queryable via S3+index), archived (7+ years offline per legal request).
- Hashing: resource identifiers are consistently hashed for cross-system correlation while preserving PII rules.

4) High-level SOC 2 / ISO 27001 control mapping (summary):
- SOC 2 CC6: Logical and physical access controls -> Evidence: RBAC policy documents, policy change log, approval tickets, role assignment audit trail (event.action=role.assign), screenshots of console role lists for sample dates.
- SOC 2 CC7: System operations and availability -> Evidence: SIEM alerts for auth anomalies, retention configuration, log pipeline architecture diagram.
- ISO 27001 A.9 (Access control) -> Evidence: RBAC v2 design doc, sample policy versions, access review cadence logs, attestations from resource owners.
- ISO 27001 A.12.4 (Logging and monitoring) -> Evidence: audit log schema spec, SIEM exports for sample windows, alerting rules and playbooks.
- Crosswalk note: include mappings to control identifiers in Confluence for exact auditor references.

5) Gap analysis (top items, concise):
- Gap 1: Evidence collection automation for role-review is manual.
  - Current state: access reviews performed quarterly using a spreadsheet exported from Console.
  - Risk: missed stale access, audit inefficiency.
  - Remediation: build automated review job that emits a per-role review artifact (who has role, last active) and push to Jira as review task. Owner: Devon Clarke. ETA: 2024-10-15.
- Gap 2: Some legacy admin events still use legacy audit schema (missing trace_id and raw_payload).
  - Current state: ~12% of admin events in July batch lack new-schema fields.
  - Risk: incomplete event correlation for audits.
  - Remediation: run a one-time migration of legacy log enrichers and backfill events from archival S3. Owner: Marcus Li. ETA: 2024-09-30.
- Gap 3: SIEM retention policy mismatch for cold archives (index not searchable).
  - Current state: cold tier stored in S3 but not indexed; auditors request samples older than 90d.
  - Risk: inability to produce historical evidence quickly.
  - Remediation: implement lightweight index snapshots for 90/180/365d windows and provide a retrieval playbook. Owner: Elena Rodriguez. ETA: 2024-11-01.
- Gap 4: No signed attestations for emergency RBAC overrides (breakglass).
  - Remediation: require post-facto approvals and attach to event.signed=true. Owner: Security Ops. ETA: 2024-09-20.

6) Auditor Q&A prep (likely questions and suggested responses)
Q: How do you prove who authorized a role change?
A: We provide policy change documents (immutable), approval ticket (Jira key) and the audit event for the role.assign containing actor_id (approver), timestamps, and policy_id linking to the document. Sample SIEM query: action:role.assign AND policy_id:PR-## AND event_ts:[2024-08-01 TO 2024-08-31].

Q: Can you show a complete trail for a failed privilege escalation attempt?
A: Yes — query authz.check with outcome:denied for actor_id=X and trace_id to correlate subsequent policy changes or alert creation. We can provide timeline artifact that includes client_ip, user_agent and related alerts.

Q: How do you ensure logs are tamper-evident?
A: Events are written to an append-only write path; we store daily manifest files with SHA256 checksums in an immutable bucket (WORM enabled) and log manifests are signed by the log writer service. Proof artifacts: manifest SHA, signed key thumbprint and S3 object versions.

Q: How is access to SIEM restricted?
A: SIEM console access is controlled via RBAC; admin roles require MFA and IP restrictions. We provide a sample role.list export and a list of SIEM admin principals.

7) Sample SIEM queries (Elastic DSL / Kibana-friendly)
- Find policy changes by author: action:policy.create OR action:policy.update AND actor_id:elena.rodriguez
- All denied authz checks for a resource in a timeframe: action:authz.check AND outcome:denied AND resource_type:project AND event_ts:[now-30d TO now]
- Role assign events lacking approval: action:role.assign AND NOT (ticket_id:*)

8) Evidence packaging checklist (for auditor request response)
- Policy design doc (RBAC v2) with changelog id
- Sample policy JSON (immutable version)
- Audit event export (NDJSON) for requested window (signed manifest)
- SIEM query output (CSV), screenshots of query and results
- Jira approvals and review tickets (redacted PII as needed)
- Hash manifest for exported files and S3 object versions
- Short narrative (1 page) that explains how items map to control IDs

9) Next steps / action items (this doc owners should track)
- Devon: prototype automated access-review emitter (proof-of-concept in repo) by 2024-09-30.
- Marcus: run schema backfill test and estimate compute cost by 2024-09-15.
- Elena: implement indexing snapshot plan for cold tier and write retrieval playbook by 2024-10-20.
- Security Ops: finalize breakglass attestation flow and update incident runbook by 2024-09-20.

Appendix: minimal reproducible evidence bundle (example):
1) NDJSON export (file: audit-export-2024-08-01.ndjson) + manifest SHA256
2) RBAC-policy-PR-118.json (immutable copy)
3) Jira ticket SEC-452 (approval flow) + screenshots
4) SIEM query: action:role.assign AND event_ts:[2024-08-01 TO 2024-08-31]

Notes and open questions:
- Confirm retention legal requirements for archived logs (legal to confirm 7y vs 3y).
- Decide whether to obfuscate resource identifiers for external auditors or grant scoped read access to raw S3 (recommended: obfuscate, provide full payload for auditor NDA only).

Status: draft. Use this document as the working checklist for the next auditor dry-run. Add links to demo exports as they are generated.

Prepared by: Aisha Patel (Security Engineering)
Reviewers: Marcus Li (Infra), Elena Rodriguez (Security Ops), Devon Clarke (Product Security)
